reference.title: Common Housing Questions
reference.shortdesc: This reference answers the most common questions about preparing your home for Cerberus.

section.title: Q: Do I need a house with a yard to adopt Cerberus?
section.p: A: Yes, Cerberus is best suited to houses with backyards to allow him to meet his daily activity needs.

section.title: Q: How long can Cerberus be left alone?
section.p: A: He should not be left alone for more than 4–5 hours without a break.

section.title: Q: Does Cerberus need a crate?
section.p: A: Yes. Cerberus can tolerate crates and occasionally sleep in crates with appropriate encouragement. A soft-sided crate or a quiet “safe area” can be used for short rest periods, but a gated room or playpen is often a better option.

section.title: Q: Can Cerberus live with cats or other small pets?
section.p: A: No, Cerberus is not compatible with cats and has a strong prey drive. Small pets must have fully secure enclosures and be closely supervised if they are in the same home. Cerberus will likely do well with a calm, balanced dog after slow, careful introductions. Success depends on the other dog’s temperament and the adopter’s ability to manage the process.

section.title: Q: How do I introduce Cerberus to children?
section.p: A: Cerberus does best in adult-only homes or with children over five years old. Always supervise interactions, teach children to respect Cerberus's space, and avoid hugging or rough play.

section.title: Q: How should I handle visitors coming to my home?
section.p: A: Cerberus can be protective of his space. Keep him leashed or behind a gate during arrivals and reward calm behavior as guests enter. Give him time to adjust at his own pace.
